At the center of Bora Özkent's agenda today was yesterday's AI-driven rally: he wrote that while the **S&P 500** rose 1.49 percent and the **Nasdaq** rose 2.26 percent, his own portfolio gained more than 3 percent in value, and that this rally was "narrow" since it was driven by a small number of stocks, but that big stock market rallies usually start out narrow like this. He reported that the download speed of **Meta**'s new AI assistant **Muse** has outpaced ChatGPT's launch, that Shopify has already formed a partnership, that Amazon, on the other hand, has resisted agents, and that this wave has spread to CPU makers, pushing **AMD**'s market cap to 1 trillion dollars. He said that for **Nvidia**, if the Trump-Xi meeting results in approval to sell H200 chips to China, there is a possibility of an additional 30 billion dollars in revenue, that energy scarcity could benefit both **Bitcoin** mining and AI data center demand, and that rocket scarcity has also created an opportunity for **Rocket Lab**. He argued that the market isn't expensive; that even though earnings expectations have risen 28.3 percent since the start of the year, the S&P's price has only risen 13.4 percent, and that the chip sector remains cheap relative to the S&P average (16.5x versus 19.4x).

He also noted that he had already closed his **SOFI** position, albeit with some difficulty. He wrote that OpenAI is projected to face a cash shortfall of roughly 278 billion dollars over 2026-2030, that this stems from its planned 856 billion dollars in infrastructure spending, and that the key question to watch is whether usage revenue will overtake costs. He reported that the share of equities in U.S. household net worth has risen to 39.9 percent, strengthening the link between stock market moves and spending appetite. In two separate posts, he shared notes on investor psychology, arguing that investors on a winning streak should avoid falling into an overconfidence trap, and that before opening a position one should build a clear thesis and avoid making up a new story once the price falls.

items.title: DNA update: up 33%

items.title: IONQ now one of his top 3 positions

items.title: Cautious take on the IONQ announcement
items.summary: jrouldz said he's happy with $IONQ's after-hours pop but stressed that today's announcement was actually a quantum simulation run on classical hardware rather than a genuine breakthrough, and that what he really wants to see are operations running on quantum hardware itself.

assets.note: Even though he's pleased with the price rally, he says the announcement was a simulation run on classical hardware, and the real excitement won't come until he sees a demonstration running on actual quantum hardware.

items.title: Defending the pace of progress in the quantum industry
items.summary: jrouldz pushed back on the skeptical view of quantum computing timelines, noting that multiple companies are targeting useful quantum computers by the early 2030s, that the sector is well capitalized, and that there's been a striking acceleration over the past two years.

assets.note: He maintains his optimism on the sector, arguing that the quantum computing industry has clearly accelerated over the past two years in both capital and timeline.

items.title: No real quantum hardware in the press release
items.summary: jrouldz said that while he agrees hybrid use will be the key application for quantum hardware, today's press release didn't actually involve any quantum hardware at all, and he'll get genuinely excited once the same operation is announced running on the 256-chip.

assets.note: He notes the announcement was a simulation run on classical systems, and says he's waiting to see the same operation demonstrated on the actual 256-qubit chip.

items.title: The demo wasn't on real hardware
items.summary: jrouldz said today's demo simulated, on classical hardware, what would theoretically be possible with a future quantum computer, that the claim "quantum hardware doesn't need to do this" is wrong, and that the ultimate goal is to actually run it on real quantum hardware.

assets.note: Stressing that the demo was a simulation run on classical hardware, he reiterates that the end goal is to actually run these operations on real quantum hardware.

items.title: In IONQ since single digits
items.summary: jrouldz said that because he's held $IONQ long-term since single-digit prices, he may have a more objective view of the stock's trajectory and achievements.

assets.note: Based on his long-held position dating back to single-digit prices, he considers himself more objective about the stock's progress.

items.title: Warning about quantum risk to Bitcoin
items.summary: jrouldz called the Bitcoin community's indifference to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) upgrades — despite the accelerating capital and timelines at quantum computing companies — the biggest bearish signal he sees, adding that while he holds a small amount of BTC, he's long stopped adding to it.

assets.note: He sees the Bitcoin network's reluctance to adopt PQC upgrades as a serious risk given how fast quantum computers are approaching the capability to break current encryption; he holds a small amount of BTC but hasn't bought more in a long time.
